gloss: contrast agent; contrast medium (for medical imaging)

definitions.explanation: A substance administered before or during a medical imaging procedure (X-ray, CT, MRI, or ultrasound) to make certain tissues or blood vessels show up more clearly on the resulting images. Common examples include iodine-based agents for X-ray/CT and gadolinium-based agents for MRI.

examples.japanese: {検査|けんさ}の{前|まえ}に{造影剤|ぞうえいざい}を{注射|ちゅうしゃ}した。
examples.english: Before the exam, they injected a contrast agent.

examples.japanese: {造影剤|ぞうえいざい}を{使|つか}うと{血管|けっかん}がはっきり{写|うつ}る。
examples.english: Using a contrast agent makes the blood vessels show up clearly.

examples.japanese: {造影剤|ぞうえいざい}に{対|たい}するアレルギーがある{方|かた}は、{事前|じぜん}にお{申|もう}し{出|で}ください。
examples.english: If you have an allergy to contrast agents, please let us know in advance.

notes:
Composed of {造影|ぞうえい} ("producing an image," from {造|つく}る + {影|えい}, originally "making a shadow" for X-ray imaging) + {剤|ざい} ("agent, preparation"). A standard medical term encountered in hospitals, on consent forms, and in health-insurance paperwork.

USAGE:
- Administered by injection, oral ingestion, or (for some imaging) by enema, depending on the exam.
- Patients are typically asked about kidney function and allergies before administration, since contrast agents can provoke allergic reactions and iodine-based agents are processed by the kidneys.
- {造影|ぞうえい} alone is also used as a verb-forming element: {造影|ぞうえい}する, "to perform contrast imaging."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {造影剤|ぞうえいざい}を{使|つか}う: to use a contrast agent
- {造影剤|ぞうえいざい}を{注射|ちゅうしゃ}する: to inject a contrast agent
- {造影剤|ぞうえいざい}アレルギー: contrast-agent allergy
- {造影剤|ぞうえいざい}の{副作用|ふくさよう}: side effects of the contrast agent
- ヨード{造影剤|ぞうえいざい}: iodine-based contrast agent

RELATED WORDS:
- {造影|ぞうえい}: contrast imaging (the procedure)
- {造影|ぞうえい}CT: contrast CT
- {造影|ぞうえい}MRI: contrast MRI
- {検査|けんさ}: examination, test
- {副作用|ふくさよう}: side effect
- アレルギー: allergy
- {注射|ちゅうしゃ}: injection
